sources.fact: Updated 13 July 2026; title plans show the general extent and normally general boundaries, and must be read with the register.
HMLR guidance separates general boundaries, determined boundaries, title plans and application-plan requirements.
INSPIRE Index Polygons metadata was updated 8 July 2026 and covers registered freehold property only.
INSPIRE polygons show indicative position and extent and use a Land Registry INSPIRE ID linked to a registered title.
Current files were published 5 July 2026; downloads are by local authority and new files are published monthly.
HMLR provides bulk geospatial datasets; INSPIRE is free while National Polygon Service is licensed/chargeable.
National Polygon Service covers freehold and leasehold titles and provides indicative title polygons with title numbers.
National Polygon geometry is an index to indicative title location; the register/title plan record general boundary position unless determined.
Search of the index map can identify title numbers where address search is insufficient and can confirm unregistered land.
The title register and title plan are authoritative title documents; rights, tenure and ownership require register-level evidence.
HMLR states the title plan shows general boundaries and unusual parcels may require map-based search.
INSPIRE is captured in British National Grid; reprojection can introduce positional shifts, with HMLR warning of shifts up to 15 metres in some conversions.

examples.result: INSPIRE polygon overlap is treated as candidate-title evidence, never exact legal boundary proof.
Freehold-only INSPIRE absence is not evidence that a leasehold title or unregistered interest is absent.
National Polygon title number linkage is retained, but polygon geometry remains indicative unless boundary determination evidence exists.
Title plan and register are required together before ownership/easement/restriction conclusions are promoted.
Reprojected INSPIRE geometry is not used for centimetre/metre boundary matching without CRS/error controls.
Index-map search is used where address/title discovery is ambiguous instead of nearest-polygon guessing.
Different historical OS mapping editions on adjoining title plans are not silently normalised into one exact boundary.
No parcel promotion occurs without exact title relation plus current title/register evidence required by the scoring gate.
